mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility supplier or regulated credit institution of the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague source states, full consular legalization of the registry certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and capital-source provenance statement from the financing UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating regulated credit institution holding the UBO's funding account

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, corporate partners, and ultimate principals against the OFAC SDN list, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list(s), and the national Luxembourg sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Finance; PEP identification of domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, immediate family members, and close associates is performed pursuant to Article 3 of the Law of 19 December 2002; enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP, high-risk third country, or complex cross-border structure; the registering agent must evidence the screening timestamp and results in the AML/CFT file before the RCS filing is transmitted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and eJustice portal via https://www.lbr.lu; electronic filing portal of the LBR
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of an SCSp may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish, or an internationally comprehensible Latin-script form, but must contain the legal-form suffix 'SCSp' without abbreviation addition; non-Latin scripts used in the commercial trade name must be accompanied by a transliteration in Latin characters; the name must be distinctive, lawful, not contrary to public order or public decency, and must not mislead the public as to the object of the company; French is the preferred registration language for the official corporate purpose description.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory pre-incorporation name-reservation book; the availability of the desired name is verified electronically on the LBR on the date of the RCS filing and is held for the SCSp by the RCS dossier number once the filing is lodged. If the LBR rejects the name, the appointed Luxembourg counsel may file up to two consecutive revised name proposals without a new signature circulation. A final rejection on grounds of public order or misleading character may be challenged by an administrative appeal lodged with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of notification of the refusal, with the Minister of Justice as the respondent; the contested name remains unusable until the court decision becomes final, and any provisional registration requires a judicial attachment order of urgency.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Domiciliation services at an approved Luxembourg registered-agent address are admissible for an SCSp for a low-risk distance e-commerce trade in custom mechanical keyboard keycaps, provided a Luxembourg-resident professional agent is appointed and the registered office is an addressable legal seat; no physical production or warehouse facility is required in the Grand Duchy, but complete accounting records, VAT files, and corporate books must be accessible in Luxembourg for direct tax and ACD inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 12% over the first three tax years for a low-risk e-commerce standard-profile SCSp; the likelihood is materially higher only if the corporate purpose is altered to a regulated financial activity, or if the tax administration detects inconsistent substance indicators, in which case a domicile visit occurs within 18 months of the first VAT registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Sections 905-1 to 905-26 inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016), and related implementing regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) / Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Deed of Formation) together with the RCS registration form and publication request
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital; contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement and may take the form of cash, in-kind, or industry services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the general partner, acting as the management body of the SCSp, hereby (1) confirms the subscription of partnership interests by the general partner and the limited partner in accordance with the partnership agreement; (2) approves the registered office of the SCSp as situated at [Address], Luxembourg; (3) appoints [Name] as gérant (Class A manager) with sole signatory authority for the SCSp and [Name] as alternate gérant; (4) authorizes the gérant to file all incorporation documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to open bank accounts, and to take all ancillary steps for operational licensing and tax registration. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary or direct private writing (for SCSp formation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft the acte constitutif (partnership agreement) in French or English, specifying the identity of the general partner and the limited partner, contributions, profit-sharing, management, and termination clauses. The agreement must be executed by all partners; if the general partner is a legal entity, its corporate authorisation must be produced. The deed may be notarized to facilitate RCS registration. File the executed deed with the RCS within one month of signing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and powers of attorney for corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises discrepancies, amend the deed and re-execute; if the RCS queries due to incomplete information, provide supplementary declarations or publish a rectification act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) – online portal: lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Luxembourg Business Registers portal and file the registration application for the newly formed SCSp. Attach the executed deed of formation, the identification forms and any exhibits (registered office certificate, list of partners). Pay the RCS filing fee and publication fee via the portal. Upon validation, the RCSL issues a registration extract bearing the RCS number.
required_dossiers: RCS registration form (Form A or B)
Identification and specimen signatures of representatives
Declaration of the general partner accepting its role
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of a query, respond via the portal within 15 days, providing corrected information or documents. If the application is rejected, rectify the defect and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) / Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the RCS registration extract to apply for a Luxembourg VAT number (if taxable transactions are expected) and a business tax reference. Since the SCSp is tax-transparent, the partners are assessed directly, but the entity must still file an annual information return (if applicable). Register any employees with the CCSS for social security and occupational health.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration objects, appeal through their internal redress procedure; provide any requested clarifications within the statutory deadline (usually 15 days).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Environnement (AAE) – Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development; local municipal authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess if the plastic-injection keycap production facility is a classified establishment under the Law of 10 June 1999. For annual plastic throughput below 100 tonnes, file a Category 2 declaration (déclaration) through the Geoportail environmental portal. Include site specifications, process description, waste management, wastewater discharge, air emissions data, and fire safety documentation. If throughput exceeds the threshold, prepare a full Category 1 EIA report and submit for opinion. Obtain the authorization before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Material Safety Data Sheets for PBT polymers
Wastewater discharge calculation and discharge permit application
Occupational risk prevention report (if employees present)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the administration requests additional studies, provide the information and feasibility reports. If the declaration is incomplete, resubmit within the grace period. If authorization is denied, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale de l'Industrie; Administration de l'Environnement (AAE) for classified establishments
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de fonctionnement pour établissement classé (Operating authorization for a classified establishment)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (AAE) – Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – Declaration (déclaration) for plastic processing facilities up to 100 t/year; Category 1 – Full EIA (autorisation) if capacity exceeds 100 t/year or if located in a sensitive area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 July 2019 on waste water discharge, with pH 6.5-9.5, COD ≤ 2000 mg/l, TSS ≤ 600 mg/l, hydrocarbons ≤ 15 mg/l; VOC emissions ≤ 50 mg C/m3 in stack; waste disposal must follow the Hazardous Waste Regulation and use authorized treatment centers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local fire brigade (including an emergency plan and fire escape routes); structural and loading approval from a licensed engineering bureau; work permit from the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) approving machinery safety, noise levels, lighting, and electrical safety before use of the injection molding equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate/income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises for customs. Central portal and e-filing: MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu; eCDF for customs formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an SCSp established in Luxembourg: (1) Register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via MyGuichet.lu to obtain the national business registration number (numéro d'identification). (2) Submit a VAT registration application (form 1000 or online e-form) to the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu, attaching the partnership agreement, proof of Luxembourg address, authority of the legal representative and projected turnover. (3) Receive the Luxembourg VAT number in the format LU followed by 8 digits (total 10 characters) and obtain an EORI number from the Customs and Excise Administration for export declarations. The SCSp may register as a VAT taxable person itself; fiscally transparent treatment for direct tax does not prevent separate VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box regime. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for corporate income tax and personal income tax; partners are taxed in their own capacity. However, an SCSp that carries on a commercial, industrial or professional activity is separately within the scope of municipal business tax (communal trade tax), and may elect for normal VAT taxation where the small business exemption would otherwise apply. A Luxembourg VAT group election (assujetti unique) is available under Luxembourg VAT law, allowing an SCSp and certain parties to be treated as a single taxable person for VAT; the election requires prior approval and is VAT-only. ATAD-based hybrid mismatch rules apply; no separate hybrid election exists under domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for the domestic small-business franchise exemption (optional; can be waived). Mandatory VAT registration applies to all taxable persons carrying out taxable activities in Luxembourg, without a de minimis turnover requirement. Non-established suppliers making distance sales of keycaps to non-taxable EU consumers must register in Luxembourg or use the Union OSS if their total cross-border distance sales exceed the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has not implemented mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping for commercial VAT invoices. E-invoicing is compulsory only for invoices addressed to public entities (B2G) under European standard EN 16931, transmitted through the national e-invoicing platform. For B2B/B2C transactions, paper or electronic invoices issued under EU VAT invoicing rules are accepted; VAT returns and EU sales listings (EC sales lists) must be filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu. SAF-T accounting data may be required during tax audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 41 of the Luxembourg Value Added Tax Act applies to the sale of custom mechanical keycaps where the goods are dispatched to a destination outside the EU and the supplier retains documentary proof of exportation. The supplier must be identified as exporter and the recipient must be located outside the EU; transport must be initiated and completed outside the EU, with transport documents evidencing departure from Luxembourg/EU. Services closely associated with the export (e.g., transport and insurance) also qualify for zero-rating. The VAT deduction remains available for input VAT incurred in making the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration (SAD / export declaration via Luxembourg Customs) including exporter of record EORI number, HS/CN code, customs value and ship or air waybill reference, with status 'exportation'
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing dispatch from the EU and arrival at the non-EU destination; for container transport, terminal or container movement reference records
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 confirmation showing the foreign customer's payment for the exported keycaps remitted to the Luxembourg bank account in the agreed foreign currency
Commercial invoice and packing list stating product description, quantity, unit values and total customs value, including Incoterms
Proof of physical departure within the period required by Luxembourg tax practice (normally within 3 months of supply), such as the export document exit confirmation or customs transit declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export zero-rating is claimed without the required substantiation, the AEDT will retroactively assess VAT at 17% on the export supply and deny input VAT recovery. The assessment window is generally five years from the end of the year in which the VAT became chargeable, extended to ten years in cases of fraud. Default interest accrues at 0.6% per month (or part month) on the unpaid VAT. Administrative fines may reach up to EUR 25,000 or, in cases of deliberate fraud, criminal penalties including imprisonment for up to five years and a criminal fine may be imposed under the Luxembourg general tax legislation. Exporters must retain the export evidence bundle for at least ten years and produce it immediately on request of the tax authorities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as the national central bank within the Eurosystem; prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment services is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the Minister of Finance retains residual regulatory authority for exchange-control policy, which is otherwise harmonised at EU level under Articles 63-66 TFEU.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility as a euro-area member. There are no residual exchange-control approvals, quantitative limits, or licensing requirements for cross-border payments, partner capital contributions, e-commerce settlement, or profit distributions by a qualifying tax-transparent SCSp. The sole operational constraints are: (i) BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting performed by resident credit institutions; (ii) source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership verification under the Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02; and (iii) payment message data requirements under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (Transfer of Funds Regulation). Profit remittance by an SCSp is treated as contractual profit-share distribution, not a dividend; no Luxembourg withholding tax applies where the SCSp has validly opted for tax transparency and no domestic anti-abuse look-through rule is triggered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg law imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio on export proceeds in foreign currency. An SCSp may retain USD, CNY, or other foreign-currency receivables in onshore or offshore accounts without BCL restriction; voluntary conversion to EUR is at the entity's discretion and is typically executed via the bank's spot or forward desk. Export receipt documentation must nevertheless support the underlying commercial transaction for AML/KYC and transfer-funds transparency purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency corporate account (EUR, USD, CNY) and partner capital escrow sub-account
Operational corporate account with trade finance (commercial LC, documentary collections) and partner capital escrow account
Operational corporate account with global payment, FX hedging, and cash-pooling treasury suite; capital escrow account available
Operational multi-currency account with cross-border clearing and trade services
Operational corporate account optimised for cooperative/domestic clearing and SEPA payments
Operational corporate account with EU-Asia trade corridors and receivables finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary payment-processing only; Low as a primary treasury bank. Luxembourg recognises CSSF-licensed Payment Institutions and E-Money Institutions, and EU/EEA EMIs may passport into Luxembourg under PSD2; however, EMIs generally cannot provide credit, offer deposit-guarantee protection (e-money floats are not covered by the EUR 100,000 FGDL scheme), or route SWIFT MT103s to non-EEA suppliers with the same certainty as a correspondent bank. For this SCSp, an EU-licensed EMI may be used as a settlement collection account for Shopify Payments and Stripe payouts, but all capital injections, trade disbursements, and FX hedges must flow through a Tier-1 Luxembourg commercial bank to preserve regulatory cleanliness.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, physical presence of the general partner (associé gérant) and at least one ultimate beneficial owner at the bank's Luxembourg branch, or a remote video-identification session accepted at the bank's discretion, is mandatory at onboarding under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF guidance. The SCSp is not a full legal personality distinct from its partners, so the account is opened in the name of the SCSp with the general partner executing the account mandate; documentary formalities include the RCS-registered partnership agreement (contrat de société), registered office certificate, list of limited partners, and partner resolutions. Pure remote opening without any human interaction is generally declined for partnerships with non-resident partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp tax-transparent structure with non-resident limited partners and no minimum legal capital, creating perceived anonymous-owner or infinite-liability red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement and RCS registration extract; registered office certificate issued by the Luxembourg service-provider; complete UBO register pursuant to CSSF Regulation 12-02; identity and KYC file of the general partner; term sheet and deed of contribution for each limited partner; tax-transparency election confirmation from a licensed Luxembourg tax advisor; substance memorandum demonstrating the SCSp's genuine commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce payment velocity from multiple heterogeneous retail payers through Shopify Payments and Stripe without treasury-grade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform merchant agreements with Shopify and Stripe; consolidated settlement statements; order-level transaction exports; payment processor payout files tied to the IBAN; commercial invoices and delivery confirmation (courier tracking or DDP customs documentation); monthly bank statement reconciliation (MT940) showing clean matching of platform net settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid onward disbursement of inbound funds to third-country contract manufacturers (PRC PBT injection-molding suppliers) without goods physically transiting Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders and supply agreements with PRC/HK manufacturers; Incoterms schedule (FOB, CIF, DDP); bill of lading / air waybill and EU customs import/export declarations (ICS/ECS or customs broker records); supplier UBO/KYC data; stock-in-transit and delivery-to-warehouse (3PL) contracts; payment schedule evidence demonstrating arm's-length pricing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential commingling of personal and corporate flows through a single SCSp account given the unlimited-liability general partner profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dedicated account mandate in the SCSp name; separate personal and corporate accounts file; general partner authorisation minutes; audited or accountant-prepared capital accounts; written confirmation that no personal expenses are drawn from the corporate account; annual financial statements for the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of EU/EEA digital EMI accounts as collection points, triggering correspondent-bank scrutiny on the ultimate origin of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passporting notification of the EMI to the CSSF; EMI licence certificate from the home state regulator (e.g., Bank of Lithuania, DNB); contractual agreements with the EMI; complete transaction waterfall from the EMI settlement account to the Tier-1 bank account; reconciliation reports proving the funds are solely e-commerce sales proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: inbound partner capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 from the partner's originating bank to the SCSp's operational account at a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. The payment must carry the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity-related transfer) or 'LOAN' (shareholder loan) where applicable, with the partnership agreement or contribution schedule number in the remittance information; the bank will file the BCL balance-of-payments statistical report for the resident partnership. Verification bundle: executed deed of contribution and subscription schedule, payment instruction matching the capital account ledger, source-of-funds evidence (partner bank statements, tax returns, or exit liquidity documentation), CSSF-compliant UBO declaration, and confirmation that the contribution is not taxable income for the tax-transparent SCSp.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer for supplier payments to PRC/HK/TW accounts, with the ISO 20022 purpose code 'GDDS' (purchase of goods for resale) or 'TRAD' (trade transaction) and the commercial invoice number in the message; (ii) commercial letters of credit (documentary credits under UCP600) advised through BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, or BCEE trade desks for high-value or recurring production orders; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer and instant SEPA for EU packaging and logistics suppliers; (iv) documentary collections (D/P or D/A) as a lower-cost alternative for mid-value orders. Platform outflows from Shopify Payments and Stripe are settled to the SCSp bank account via SEPA or SWIFT credit in EUR/USD; concentration of all payables through one Tier-1 account ensures MT940 reconciliation and clean FX marking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD spot and outright deliverable forward contracts (tenor-matched to payment cycles) documented under an ISDA 1992/2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex, available from BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, and BCEE treasury desks
FX swaps and rollover swaps for short-term liquidity management between EUR and USD
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for long-term structural hedging of recurring platform revenue and supplier-cost cycles, subject to EMIR reporting to an EU-authorised trade repository

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNH/USD or CNH/EUR for hedging PRC supplier cost exposures where onshore deliverable CNY forwards cannot be settled by the SCSp without underlying trade documentation; NDFs are permitted under Luxembourg law and are typically executed with the bank's offshore CNY desk
Vanilla FX options (EUR/USD and CNH/EUR) for asymmetric risk protection; permissible under MiFID II, requiring an appropriateness assessment and EMIR margin documentation if uncleared

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE / UBO register) data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the calendar year; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 1,250 and imprisonment up to 6 months under the law of 13 January 2019; subsequent default may be made public.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) where statutory thresholds are met or exemption is lost
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the balance-sheet date (e.g., by 31 July following a 31 December year-end). SCSp is generally exempt unless the undertaking exceeds large-entity thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, or average employees above 50.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 1,500 per omission; court order may compel filing and expose the partnership to criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and publication of non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS maintenance fee (droit annuel de maintien au registre)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and potential suspension of RCS registration; persistent non-payment may lead to administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual taxable transparency declaration for partnerships (déclaration de la société de personnes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, generally by 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end for electronically filed returns, subject to the official tax assessment letter; paper filings follow the published filing calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty of 0.6% of the net tax due, default interest, and administrative tax assessment on a fixed basis; intentional failure may trigger criminal fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SCSp is generally exempt from statutory audit unless: (i) it exceeds the large-undertaking thresholds (balance sheet > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, average employees > 50); (ii) it is a regulated financial undertaking, an alternative investment fund, or a public-interest entity; (iii) it controls one or more subsidiaries requiring consolidated accounts; or (iv) the partnership agreement or partners’ resolution mandates an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 15 December 2010 on accounting obligations and the Luxembourg Commercial Code; IFRS is optional for non-listed undertakings and permitted for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file the identity of all ultimate beneficial owners with the RBE upon registration and within one month of any change. An annual confirmation duty applies to verify the accuracy of RBE data as at year-end; the entity must review partner-level ownership and control, including transfers of partnership interests, and update statutory registers accordingly. Non-compliance is subject to fines and publication measures.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (associés) and partnership interests
Register of general partners (commandités) and supervisory partners, if any
Minute book of partner resolutions and meetings
Locally available copy or extract of the RBE beneficial ownership declaration

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,500 per annum for a Luxembourg registered office and corporate domiciliation agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 15,000 per annum for a small or medium SCSp, dependent on transaction volume, subsidiary structure, and audit scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + municipal business tax (6.75% in Luxembourg City) = 24.94% combined headline
